text: I am forever walking upon these shores, Betwixt the sand and the foam. The high tide will erase my foot-prints, And the wind will blow away the foam. But the sea and the shore will remain Forever.
note: Transience of our traces; what endures

tags.when_helps: For someone feeling their traces are fleeting, steadied by what endures.

display_text: I am forever walking upon these shores, Betwixt the sand and the foam. The high tide will erase my foot-prints, And the wind will blow away the foam. But the sea and the shore will remain Forever.
plain: I walk forever along these shores between the sand and the foam. The tide will erase my footprints and the wind will blow the foam away, but the sea and shore will remain forever.
core_idea: Our traces fade; the sea and shore remain

text: It was but yesterday I thought myself a fragment quivering without rhythm in the sphere of life. Now I know that I am the sphere, and all life in rhythmic fragments moves within me.
note: From feeling fragmentary to feeling whole

tags.when_helps: For someone who feels like a meaningless fragment and needs to sense their wholeness.

display_text: It was but yesterday I thought myself a fragment quivering without rhythm in the sphere of life. Now I know that I am the sphere, and all life in rhythmic fragments moves within me.
plain: Only yesterday I thought I was a fragment trembling out of rhythm in life. Now I know I am the whole sphere, and all life moves within me in rhythmic fragments.
core_idea: You are not a fragment; life moves within you

text: They say to me in their awakening, “You and the world you live in are but a grain of sand upon the infinite shore of an infinite sea.” And in my dream I say to them, “I am the infinite sea, and all worlds are but grains of sand upon my shore.”
note: Feeling small versus feeling vast inside

tags.when_helps: For someone made to feel insignificant who needs to sense the vastness within.

display_text: They say to me in their awakening, “You and the world you live in are but a grain of sand upon the infinite shore of an infinite sea.” And in my dream I say to them, “I am the infinite sea, and all worlds are but grains of sand upon my shore.”
plain: Awake, people tell me I and my world are a grain of sand on an infinite shore. In my dream I tell them I am the infinite sea, and all worlds are grains of sand on my shore.
core_idea: You are the sea, not the grain of sand

text: Only once have I been made mute. It was when a man asked me, “Who are you?”
note: Struggling to say who you really are

tags.when_helps: For someone stumped by the question of who they really are.

display_text: Only once have I been made mute. It was when a man asked me, “Who are you?”
plain: Only once have I been left speechless: when someone asked me who I am.
core_idea: The hardest question is who you are

text: A pearl is a temple built by pain around a grain of sand. What longing built our bodies and around what grains?

tags.when_helps: For someone in pain who wonders whether something beautiful could grow from it.

display_text: A pearl is a temple built by pain around a grain of sand. What longing built our bodies and around what grains?
plain: A pearl is a temple that pain builds around a grain of sand. What longing built our bodies, and around what grains?
core_idea: Pain and longing build beautiful things

text: When God threw me, a pebble, into this wondrous lake I disturbed its surface with countless circles. But when I reached the depths I became very still.
note: Restlessness on the surface, stillness in depth

tags.when_helps: For someone churning on the surface who needs to sense the stillness in their depths.

display_text: When God threw me, a pebble, into this wondrous lake I disturbed its surface with countless circles. But when I reached the depths I became very still.
plain: When God threw me like a pebble into this wonderful lake, I stirred its surface with countless circles. But when I reached the depths, I became very still.
core_idea: Depth brings stillness after surface turmoil

text: Give me silence and I will outdare the night.
note: Silence as a source of courage

tags.when_helps: For someone facing a frightening night who draws strength from silence.

display_text: Give me silence and I will outdare the night.
plain: Give me silence, and I will be bolder than the night.
core_idea: Silence gives courage to face the dark

text: I had a second birth when my soul and my body loved one another and were married.
note: Making peace between body and soul

tags.when_helps: For someone at odds with their body, or newly at peace with it.

display_text: I had a second birth when my soul and my body loved one another and were married.
plain: I was born a second time when my soul and my body loved each other and became one.
core_idea: Soul and body united bring rebirth

text: Remembrance is a form of meeting. Forgetfulness is a form of freedom.
note: Remembering and forgetting those we have lost

tags.when_helps: For someone torn between holding on to a memory and letting it go.

display_text: Remembrance is a form of meeting. Forgetfulness is a form of freedom.
plain: Remembering is a kind of meeting. Forgetting is a kind of freedom.
core_idea: Memory reunites; forgetting frees

text: Do not the spirits who dwell in the ether envy man his pain?
note: Pain as something precious about being human

tags.when_helps: For someone in pain who might see suffering as part of being fully human.

display_text: Do not the spirits who dwell in the ether envy man his pain?
plain: Don't the spirits living in the sky envy humans their pain?
core_idea: Pain may be a gift even spirits envy

text: On my way to the Holy City I met another pilgrim and I asked him, “Is this indeed the way to the Holy City?” And he said, “Follow me, and you will reach the Holy City in a day and a night.” And I followed him. And we walked many days and many nights, yet we did not reach the Holy City. And what was to my surprise he became angry with me because he had misled me.
note: Being misled, then blamed by the one who misled

tags.when_helps: For someone misled by a guide who then blamed them for it.

display_text: On my way to the Holy City I met another pilgrim and I asked him, “Is this indeed the way to the Holy City?” And he said, “Follow me, and you will reach the Holy City in a day and a night.” And I followed him. And we walked many days and many nights, yet we did not reach the Holy City. And what was to my surprise he became angry with me because he had misled me.
plain: A pilgrim told me to follow him to the Holy City in a day and a night. We walked many days and nights without reaching it, and to my surprise he grew angry with me because he had misled me.
core_idea: Those who mislead us often blame us for it

text: Make me, oh God, the prey of the lion, ere You make the rabbit my prey.
note: Preferring to be wronged than to wrong others

tags.when_helps: For someone tempted to prey on the weak, who would rather suffer than harm.

display_text: Make me, oh God, the prey of the lion, ere You make the rabbit my prey.
plain: God, let me be the lion's prey before you let the rabbit be mine.
core_idea: Better to be prey than prey on the weak

text: One may not reach the dawn save by the path of the night.
note: Hard times as the path to better ones

tags.when_helps: For someone in a dark stretch who needs to hear the dawn comes through it.

display_text: One may not reach the dawn save by the path of the night.
plain: You can reach the dawn only by going through the night.
core_idea: Only through darkness do we reach the dawn

text: My house says to me, “Do not leave me, for here dwells your past.” And the road says to me, “Come and follow me, for I am your future.” And I say to both my house and the road, “I have no past, nor have I a future. If I stay here, there is a going in my staying; and if I go there is a staying in my going. Only love and death change all things.”
note: Torn between past and future; staying or going

tags.when_helps: For someone torn between staying and leaving, caught between past and future.

display_text: My house says to me, “Do not leave me, for here dwells your past.” And the road says to me, “Come and follow me, for I am your future.” And I say to both my house and the road, “I have no past, nor have I a future. If I stay here, there is a going in my staying; and if I go there is a staying in my going. Only love and death change all things.”
plain: My house begs me to stay with my past; the road calls me to my future. I tell them I have neither: in staying there is going, in going there is staying. Only love and death change everything.
core_idea: Only love and death truly change things

text: How can I lose faith in the justice of life, when the dreams of those who sleep upon feathers are not more beautiful than the dreams of those who sleep upon the earth?
note: Trusting life's fairness; rich and poor alike dream

tags.when_helps: Someone resenting that others have more comfort or wealth, and starting to doubt that life is fair.

display_text: How can I lose faith in the justice of life, when the dreams of those who sleep upon feathers are not more beautiful than the dreams of those who sleep upon the earth?
plain: How can I lose faith in life's fairness, when those who sleep on feathers dream no more beautifully than those who sleep on the bare ground?
core_idea: Dreams are equal for rich and poor

text: Strange, the desire for certain pleasures is a part of my pain.

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone noticing that their own wanting for certain pleasures is what keeps hurting them.

display_text: Strange, the desire for certain pleasures is a part of my pain.
plain: Strangely, wanting certain pleasures is part of my pain.
core_idea: Desire itself can be a source of pain

text: Seven times have I despised my soul: The first time when I saw her being meek that she might attain height. The second time when I saw her limping before the crippled. The third time when she was given to choose between the hard and the easy, and she chose the easy. The fourth time when she committed a wrong, and comforted herself that others also commit wrong. The fifth time when she forbore for weakness, and attributed her patience to strength. The sixth time when she despised the ugliness of a face, and knew not that it was one of her own masks. And the seventh time when she sang a song of praise, and deemed it a virtue.
note: Honest self-examination of one's own failings

tags.when_helps: Someone ready for honest self-examination of their hidden excuses, vanity and moral shortcuts.

display_text: Seven times have I despised my soul: The first time when I saw her being meek that she might attain height. The second time when I saw her limping before the crippled. The third time when she was given to choose between the hard and the easy, and she chose the easy. The fourth time when she committed a wrong, and comforted herself that others also commit wrong. The fifth time when she forbore for weakness, and attributed her patience to strength. The sixth time when she despised the ugliness of a face, and knew not that it was one of her own masks. And the seventh time when she sang a song of praise, and deemed it a virtue.
plain: I have despised my soul seven times: when it was meek to rise, limped before the lame, chose the easy, excused its wrong by others', called weakness patience, scorned a face that was its own mask, and prized its praise-song.
core_idea: Seven ways the soul betrays itself

text: I am ignorant of absolute truth. But I am humble before my ignorance and therein lies my honor and my reward.
note: Humility about what we do not know

tags.when_helps: Someone uneasy about how little they really know, needing permission to be humble rather than ashamed.

display_text: I am ignorant of absolute truth. But I am humble before my ignorance and therein lies my honor and my reward.
plain: I do not know absolute truth, but I am humble about my ignorance, and that humility is my honour and reward.
core_idea: Humility before ignorance is its own honour

text: There is a space between man's imagination and man's attainment that may only be traversed by his longing.

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone frustrated by the gap between what they imagine for themselves and what they have achieved.

display_text: There is a space between man's imagination and man's attainment that may only be traversed by his longing.
plain: Between what we imagine and what we achieve lies a gap that only our longing can cross.
core_idea: Longing bridges imagination and achievement

text: Paradise is there, behind that door, in the next room; but I have lost the key. Perhaps I have only mislaid it.
note: Feeling locked out of happiness, with hope

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels happiness or grace is close yet out of reach, and fears it is gone for good.

display_text: Paradise is there, behind that door, in the next room; but I have lost the key. Perhaps I have only mislaid it.
plain: Paradise is just behind that door, in the next room, but I have lost the key. Maybe I have only misplaced it.
core_idea: Paradise is near; we've only mislaid the key

text: You are blind and I am deaf and dumb, so let us touch hands and understand.

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone struggling to communicate with another person, needing to reach for connection beyond words.

display_text: You are blind and I am deaf and dumb, so let us touch hands and understand.
plain: You are blind and I cannot hear or speak, so let us touch hands and understand each other.
core_idea: Understanding can pass beyond words and sight

text: The significance of man is not in what he attains, but rather in what he longs to attain.
note: Worth lies in aspiration, not achievement

tags.when_helps: Someone measuring their worth by achievements and feeling they have fallen short.

display_text: The significance of man is not in what he attains, but rather in what he longs to attain.
plain: A person's meaning lies not in what they achieve but in what they long to achieve.
core_idea: We are defined by our longings, not achievements

text: Some of us are like ink and some like paper. And if it were not for the blackness of some of us, some of us would be dumb; And if it were not for the whiteness of some of us, some of us would be blind.

tags.when_helps: Someone judging others as too different, or feeling their own darker side has no use.

display_text: Some of us are like ink and some like paper. And if it were not for the blackness of some of us, some of us would be dumb; And if it were not for the whiteness of some of us, some of us would be blind.
plain: Some of us are like ink and some like paper. Without the dark ones, some would have no voice; without the light ones, some could not see.
core_idea: We need each other's differences to be seen and heard

text: Give me an ear and I will give you a voice.
note: Listening that gives others a voice

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels unheard, or who wants to become a better listener to others.

display_text: Give me an ear and I will give you a voice.
plain: If you listen to me, I will give you a voice.
core_idea: Listening is repaid with a voice

text: Our mind is a sponge; our heart is a stream. Is it not strange that most of us choose sucking rather than running?

tags.when_helps: Someone stuck in their head, absorbing and analysing, rather than letting feeling flow outward.

display_text: Our mind is a sponge; our heart is a stream. Is it not strange that most of us choose sucking rather than running?
plain: Our mind is like a sponge and our heart like a stream. Isn't it strange that most of us choose to soak things up rather than to flow?
core_idea: Choose to flow like the heart, not absorb

text: When you long for blessings that you may not name, and when you grieve knowing not the cause, then indeed you are growing with all things that grow, and rising toward your greater self.
note: Nameless longing and grief as growth

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling sad or yearning without knowing why, who needs to see it as a sign of growth.

display_text: When you long for blessings that you may not name, and when you grieve knowing not the cause, then indeed you are growing with all things that grow, and rising toward your greater self.
plain: When you yearn for good things you cannot name, and feel sad without knowing why, you are growing along with everything that grows and rising toward a larger self.
core_idea: Nameless longing and sorrow are signs of growth

text: When my cup is empty I resign myself to its emptiness; but when it is half full I resent its half-fulness.

tags.when_helps: Someone who notices that having part of what they want leaves them more dissatisfied than having nothing.

display_text: When my cup is empty I resign myself to its emptiness; but when it is half full I resent its half-fulness.
plain: When my cup is empty I accept it, but when it is only half full I resent that it is not full.
core_idea: Partial having breeds more resentment than having nothing

text: The reality of the other person is not in what he reveals to you, but in what he cannot reveal to you. Therefore, if you would understand him, listen not to what he says but rather to what he does not say.
note: Understanding others through what they cannot say

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone struggling to understand a partner, friend or relative who will not open up.

display_text: The reality of the other person is not in what he reveals to you, but in what he cannot reveal to you. Therefore, if you would understand him, listen not to what he says but rather to what he does not say.
plain: What is real in another person lies in what they cannot show you, so to understand them, listen to what they leave unsaid.
core_idea: Understand people by what they cannot say

text: Half of what I say is meaningless; but I say it so that the other half may reach you.

tags.when_helps: Someone frustrated that they cannot express themselves well, or worried their words fall flat.

display_text: Half of what I say is meaningless; but I say it so that the other half may reach you.
plain: Half of what I say means nothing, but I say it so the other half can get through to you.
core_idea: Some words exist to carry the meaningful ones

text: A sense of humor is a sense of proportion.

tags.when_helps: Someone taking a setback too seriously who needs help seeing it in proportion.

display_text: A sense of humor is a sense of proportion.
plain: Having a sense of humour means seeing things in their right proportion.
core_idea: Humour is a sense of proportion

text: My loneliness was born when men praised my talkative faults and blamed my silent virtues.
note: Loneliness from being valued for the wrong things

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling misunderstood, praised for the wrong things and overlooked for their quiet strengths.

display_text: My loneliness was born when men praised my talkative faults and blamed my silent virtues.
plain: My loneliness began when people praised my chatty faults and criticised my quiet virtues.
core_idea: Being praised for faults and blamed for virtues isolates

text: A truth is to be known always, to be uttered sometimes.
note: Knowing when to speak a truth

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone torn about whether to say a hard truth out loud right now.

display_text: A truth is to be known always, to be uttered sometimes.
plain: A truth should always be known, but only sometimes spoken.
core_idea: Know truth always; speak it only sometimes

text: The real in us is silent; the acquired is talkative.
note: True self is quiet; the acquired is noisy

tags.when_helps: Someone tired of their own noise and performance, looking for what is genuine in them.

display_text: The real in us is silent; the acquired is talkative.
plain: The real part of us is quiet; the part we have picked up from outside is the part that talks.
core_idea: Our true self is silent, the acquired self talks

text: The voice of life in me cannot reach the ear of life in you; but let us talk that we may not feel lonely.
note: Talking to ease loneliness despite distance

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling that no one can truly understand them, yet still wanting company.

display_text: The voice of life in me cannot reach the ear of life in you; but let us talk that we may not feel lonely.
plain: The life in me cannot truly reach the life in you, but let us talk anyway so we do not feel alone.
core_idea: We talk to ease loneliness, though words cannot fully connect

plain_judge.issue: "Cannot truly reach" softens the flat "cannot reach".

text: Only the dumb envy the talkative.
note: Envy of those who speak easily

tags.when_helps: A quiet person envying those who speak easily and draw attention.

display_text: Only the dumb envy the talkative.
plain: Only those who cannot speak are jealous of those who talk a lot.
core_idea: Only the voiceless envy the talkative

text: If winter should say, “Spring is in my heart,” who would believe winter?
note: Words that contradict how someone seems

tags.when_helps: Someone in a bleak season of life whose inner hope others cannot yet see or believe.

display_text: If winter should say, “Spring is in my heart,” who would believe winter?
plain: If winter claimed to have spring in its heart, who would believe it?
core_idea: Claims that contradict appearances are hard to believe

text: Should you really open your eyes and see, you would behold your image in all images. And should you open your ears and listen, you would hear your own voice in all voices.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling separate from others, open to seeing themselves reflected in everyone.

display_text: Should you really open your eyes and see, you would behold your image in all images. And should you open your ears and listen, you would hear your own voice in all voices.
plain: If you truly looked, you would see yourself in everything you see, and if you truly listened, you would hear your own voice in every voice.
core_idea: You can find yourself in everyone and everything

text: It takes two of us to discover truth: one to utter it and one to understand it.
note: Truth needs both speaker and listener

tags.when_helps: Someone frustrated at not being understood, or who values the listener in any conversation.

display_text: It takes two of us to discover truth: one to utter it and one to understand it.
plain: Finding truth takes two people: one to say it and one to understand it.
core_idea: Truth needs a speaker and a listener

text: Many a doctrine is like a window pane. We see truth through it but it divides us from truth.
note: Beliefs that both reveal and divide

tags.when_helps: Someone questioning rigid religious teaching while still seeking truth.

display_text: Many a doctrine is like a window pane. We see truth through it but it divides us from truth.
plain: Many beliefs are like a window: you see the truth through them, but they also keep you apart from it.
core_idea: Doctrines reveal truth yet separate us from it

text: Now let us play hide and seek. Should you hide in my heart it would not be difficult to find you. But should you hide behind your own shell, then it would be useless for anyone to seek you.
note: Hiding behind defences makes us unreachable

tags.when_helps: Someone who keeps others out and wonders why they feel unreachable.

display_text: Now let us play hide and seek. Should you hide in my heart it would not be difficult to find you. But should you hide behind your own shell, then it would be useless for anyone to seek you.
plain: Let us play hide and seek: if you hid in my heart you would be easy to find, but if you hide inside your own shell, no one can find you.
core_idea: Hiding behind your defences makes you unreachable

text: How noble is the sad heart who would sing a joyous song with joyous hearts.

tags.when_helps: Someone sad inside who still shows up wholeheartedly for other people's happiness.

display_text: How noble is the sad heart who would sing a joyous song with joyous hearts.
plain: How noble is a sad heart that will join happy hearts in singing a happy song.
core_idea: It is noble to share joy while sad

text: I would walk with all those who walk. I would not stand still to watch the procession passing by.
note: Participating in life rather than watching

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to watch life from the sidelines rather than join in.

display_text: I would walk with all those who walk. I would not stand still to watch the procession passing by.
plain: I want to walk along with everyone who is walking, not stand still and watch the procession go past.
core_idea: Join life rather than watch it pass

text: You owe more than gold to him who serves you. Give him of your heart or serve him.
note: Owing kindness, not just pay, to those who serve

tags.when_helps: Someone who relies on others' service or employs people and wants to treat them with real care.

display_text: You owe more than gold to him who serves you. Give him of your heart or serve him.
plain: You owe the person who serves you more than money: give them your heart, or serve them in return.
core_idea: Those who serve us deserve heart, not just pay

text: Trees are poems that the earth writes upon the sky. We fell them down and turn them into paper that we may record our emptiness.

tags.when_helps: Someone who loves nature and feels the hollowness of a busy, paper-filled life.

display_text: Trees are poems that the earth writes upon the sky. We fell them down and turn them into paper that we may record our emptiness.
plain: Trees are poems the earth writes on the sky, and we cut them down to make paper so we can write down our emptiness.
core_idea: We destroy natural poetry to record our emptiness

text: If I were to choose between the power of writing a poem and the ecstasy of a poem unwritten, I would choose the ecstasy. It is better poetry.

tags.when_helps: Someone who values the inner experience of inspiration more than producing finished results.

display_text: If I were to choose between the power of writing a poem and the ecstasy of a poem unwritten, I would choose the ecstasy. It is better poetry.
plain: Given the choice between the power to write a poem and the joy of a poem never written, I would choose the joy, because it is the better poetry.
core_idea: The unwritten poem's ecstasy is better poetry

text: Poetry is not an opinion expressed. It is a song that rises from a bleeding wound or a smiling mouth.
note: Art born from pain or joy

tags.when_helps: Someone who wants to turn deep pain or joy into creative expression.

display_text: Poetry is not an opinion expressed. It is a song that rises from a bleeding wound or a smiling mouth.
plain: Poetry is not stating an opinion; it is a song that comes from a painful wound or a smiling mouth.
core_idea: Poetry is song born of pain or joy

text: If you sing of beauty though alone in the heart of the desert you will have an audience.

tags.when_helps: An artist or maker working without an audience who wonders whether it matters.

display_text: If you sing of beauty though alone in the heart of the desert you will have an audience.
plain: If you sing about beauty, even all alone in the middle of a desert, someone will hear you.
core_idea: Singing of beauty always finds an audience

text: Poetry is wisdom that enchants the heart. Wisdom is poetry that sings in the mind.
note: Poetry and wisdom, heart and mind

tags.when_helps: Someone who loves poetry and ideas and enjoys seeing how the two meet.

display_text: Poetry is wisdom that enchants the heart. Wisdom is poetry that sings in the mind.
plain: Poetry is wisdom that delights the heart, and wisdom is poetry that sings in the mind.
core_idea: Poetry and wisdom are two faces of one thing

text: We often sing lullabyes to our children that we ourselves may sleep.

tags.when_helps: A tired parent who notices that soothing their child also soothes themselves.

display_text: We often sing lullabyes to our children that we ourselves may sleep.
plain: We often sing lullabies to our children so that we ourselves can get to sleep.
core_idea: What we do for others often soothes ourselves

text: A great singer is he who sings our silences.

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels deeply understood by music or art that says what they cannot.

display_text: A great singer is he who sings our silences.
plain: A great singer is one who gives voice to what we keep silent.
core_idea: Great singers voice our silences

text: How can you sing if your mouth be filled with food? How shall your hand be raised in blessing if it is filled with gold?

tags.when_helps: Someone with plenty who senses that comfort and wealth are dulling their spirit and generosity.

display_text: How can you sing if your mouth be filled with food? How shall your hand be raised in blessing if it is filled with gold?
plain: How can you sing with a mouth full of food, or raise your hand to bless when it is full of gold?
core_idea: Fullness and greed block song and blessing

text: They say the nightingale pierces his bosom with a thorn when he sings his love song. So do we all. How else should we sing?
note: Love and creativity born of pain

tags.when_helps: Someone aching from love who needs to know that pain is part of how love finds its voice.

display_text: They say the nightingale pierces his bosom with a thorn when he sings his love song. So do we all. How else should we sing?
plain: People say the nightingale presses a thorn into its breast when it sings its love song; we all do the same, for how else could we sing?
core_idea: All true song comes from pain

text: Even the most winged spirit cannot escape physical necessity.
note: Limits of the body even for lofty spirits

tags.when_helps: Someone frustrated that their body's needs or limits hold back their higher ambitions.

display_text: Even the most winged spirit cannot escape physical necessity.
plain: Even the most free and soaring spirit still has bodily needs it cannot escape.
core_idea: No spirit escapes physical needs

text: A madman is not less a musician than you or myself; only the instrument on which he plays is a little out of tune.
note: Compassion for mental illness and difference

tags.when_helps: Someone living with mental illness, or loving someone who is, who feels judged as less than others.

display_text: A madman is not less a musician than you or myself; only the instrument on which he plays is a little out of tune.
plain: A mad person is just as much a musician as you or I; only their instrument is a little out of tune.
core_idea: The mad share our music, slightly out of tune

text: The song that lies silent in the heart of a mother sings upon the lips of her child.
note: What parents carry passes to children

tags.when_helps: A parent who sees their own unlived hopes coming alive in their child.

display_text: The song that lies silent in the heart of a mother sings upon the lips of her child.
plain: The song a mother keeps silent in her heart is sung out loud by her child.
core_idea: A mother's hidden song lives in her child

text: No longing remains unfulfilled.
note: Hope that longing is never wasted

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone yearning for something that seems out of reach, who needs reassurance to keep hoping.

display_text: No longing remains unfulfilled.
plain: Every longing is eventually fulfilled.
core_idea: No longing stays unfulfilled

plain_judge.issue: Adds "eventually", a timing the passage does not state.

text: I have never agreed with my other self wholly. The truth of the matter seems to lie between us.
note: Inner conflict and finding the middle ground

tags.when_helps: Someone torn between two sides of themselves and unable to settle on either.

display_text: I have never agreed with my other self wholly. The truth of the matter seems to lie between us.
plain: I have never fully agreed with my other self; the truth seems to lie somewhere between us.
core_idea: Truth lies between our inner selves

text: Your other self is always sorry for you. But your other self grows on sorrow; so all is well.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling sorry for themselves who can come to see sorrow as soil for growth.

display_text: Your other self is always sorry for you. But your other self grows on sorrow; so all is well.
plain: Your other self always feels sorry for you, but it grows by sorrow, so all is well.
core_idea: Your other self grows through sorrow

text: There is no struggle of soul and body save in the minds of those whose souls are asleep and whose bodies are out of tune.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling torn between spiritual ideals and bodily appetites.

display_text: There is no struggle of soul and body save in the minds of those whose souls are asleep and whose bodies are out of tune.
plain: Soul and body only seem to fight in people whose souls are asleep and whose bodies are out of tune.
core_idea: Soul and body conflict only when out of balance

text: When you reach the heart of life you shall find beauty in all things, even in the eyes that are blind to beauty.

tags.when_helps: Someone who has stopped seeing beauty in people or the world and wants to find it again.

display_text: When you reach the heart of life you shall find beauty in all things, even in the eyes that are blind to beauty.
plain: When you reach the heart of life you will find beauty in everything, even in eyes that cannot see beauty.
core_idea: At life's heart, everything holds beauty

text: We live only to discover beauty. All else is a form of waiting.

tags.when_helps: Someone asking what life is for, open to a simple and hopeful answer.

display_text: We live only to discover beauty. All else is a form of waiting.
plain: We live only to discover beauty; everything else is a kind of waiting.
core_idea: Life's purpose is discovering beauty

text: Sow a seed and the earth will yield you a flower. Dream your dream to the sky and it will bring you your beloved.
note: Hope: dreams bring what we love

tags.when_helps: Someone dreaming of love or a hoped-for future who needs encouragement to keep dreaming.

display_text: Sow a seed and the earth will yield you a flower. Dream your dream to the sky and it will bring you your beloved.
plain: Plant a seed and the earth will give you a flower; dream your dream to the sky and it will bring you the one you love.
core_idea: What you sow and dream returns to you

text: The devil died the very day you were born. Now you do not have to go through hell to meet an angel.

tags.when_helps: Someone who believes they must suffer or prove themselves before they can find goodness.

display_text: The devil died the very day you were born. Now you do not have to go through hell to meet an angel.
plain: The devil died the day you were born, so now you do not have to pass through hell to meet an angel.
core_idea: You need not go through hell to find goodness

text: If you would possess you must not claim.

tags.when_helps: Someone gripping a person or thing too tightly out of fear of losing it.

display_text: If you would possess you must not claim.
plain: If you want to possess something, you must not lay claim to it.
core_idea: To possess, do not claim

text: When a man’s hand touches the hand of a woman they both touch the heart of eternity.
note: The sacredness of touch between lovers

tags.when_helps: Someone newly in love, feeling touched by something larger than themselves.

display_text: When a man’s hand touches the hand of a woman they both touch the heart of eternity.
plain: When a man and a woman touch hands, they both touch the heart of eternity.
core_idea: A lovers' touch reaches eternity

text: Love is the veil between lover and lover.
note: Love itself as a veil between lovers

tags.when_helps: Someone in love who still feels a distance from their partner they cannot explain.

display_text: Love is the veil between lover and lover.
plain: Love itself is the veil that hangs between two lovers.
core_idea: Love both joins and veils lovers

text: Men who do not forgive women their little faults will never enjoy their great virtues.
note: Forgiving small faults in a partner

tags.when_helps: Someone fixated on a partner's small flaws and missing their larger goodness.

display_text: Men who do not forgive women their little faults will never enjoy their great virtues.
plain: Men who will not forgive women their small faults will never get to enjoy their great virtues.
core_idea: Forgive small faults to enjoy great virtues

text: Love that does not renew itself every day becomes a habit and in turn a slavery.
note: Keeping love fresh rather than habitual

tags.when_helps: Someone in a long relationship that has slipped into routine and obligation.

display_text: Love that does not renew itself every day becomes a habit and in turn a slavery.
plain: Love that is not made new every day turns into a habit, and then into a kind of slavery.
core_idea: Love must be renewed daily or it enslaves

text: Lovers embrace that which is between them rather than each other.

tags.when_helps: Someone wondering whether they love their partner or only the idea of the relationship.

display_text: Lovers embrace that which is between them rather than each other.
plain: Lovers embrace what lies between them rather than each other.
core_idea: Lovers embrace their bond, not each other

text: Love and doubt have never been on speaking terms.

tags.when_helps: Someone doubting a partner or relationship and wondering what that doubt says about the love.

display_text: Love and doubt have never been on speaking terms.
plain: Love and doubt have never been on speaking terms with each other.
core_idea: Love and doubt cannot coexist

text: Friendship is always a sweet responsibility, never an opportunity.

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone reconsidering what they owe a friend, or feeling a friend is using them.

display_text: Friendship is always a sweet responsibility, never an opportunity.
plain: Friendship is always a sweet duty, never a chance to gain something.
core_idea: Friendship is responsibility, not opportunity

text: If you do not understand your friend under all conditions you will never understand him.

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone struggling with a friend who is behaving differently in hard times.

display_text: If you do not understand your friend under all conditions you will never understand him.
plain: If you do not understand your friend in every kind of situation, you will never understand them.
core_idea: Truly knowing a friend means knowing them in all conditions

text: Your most radiant garment is of the other person’s weaving; Your most savory meal is that which you eat at the other person’s table; Your most comfortable bed is in the other person’s house. Now tell me, how can you separate yourself from the other person?
note: Interdependence: our best comes from others

tags.when_helps: Someone proud of their independence, or feeling cut off, who needs to see how much they depend on others.

display_text: Your most radiant garment is of the other person’s weaving; Your most savory meal is that which you eat at the other person’s table; Your most comfortable bed is in the other person’s house. Now tell me, how can you separate yourself from the other person?
plain: Your finest clothes are woven by others, your tastiest meal is at another's table, your most comfortable bed is in another's house; so how can you separate yourself from other people?
core_idea: We cannot separate ourselves from others

text: Your mind and my heart will never agree until your mind ceases to live in numbers and my heart in the mist.
note: Head and heart failing to agree

tags.when_helps: Someone in a relationship where one leads with logic and the other with feeling.

display_text: Your mind and my heart will never agree until your mind ceases to live in numbers and my heart in the mist.
plain: Your mind and my heart will never agree until your mind stops living in numbers and my heart stops living in fog.
core_idea: Mind and heart agree only when both leave extremes

text: How shall my heart be unsealed unless it be broken?

tags.when_helps: Someone heartbroken who needs to see their pain as an opening rather than an end.

display_text: How shall my heart be unsealed unless it be broken?
plain: How can my heart be opened unless it is broken?
core_idea: A heart opens only when broken

text: Only great sorrow or great joy can reveal your truth.
note: Sorrow and joy reveal who we are

tags.when_helps: Someone in an intense season of pain or happiness, discovering who they really are.

display_text: Only great sorrow or great joy can reveal your truth.
plain: Only great sorrow or great joy can show who you really are.
core_idea: Great sorrow or joy reveals your truth

text: If you would be revealed you must either dance naked in the sun, or carry your cross.
note: Being truly seen requires joy or suffering

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid to be truly seen, weighing open joy against painful trial as ways to be known.

display_text: If you would be revealed you must either dance naked in the sun, or carry your cross.
plain: If you want to be truly seen, you must either dance freely and openly in the sun or carry your cross.
core_idea: You are revealed through joy or suffering

plain_judge.issue: "Dance freely and openly" softens "dance naked", losing the full exposure.

text: Should nature heed what we say of contentment no river would seek the sea, and no winter would turn to Spring. Should she heed all we say of thrift, how many of us would be breathing this air?

tags.when_helps: Someone told to be content who feels a natural drive to keep moving and seeking.

display_text: Should nature heed what we say of contentment no river would seek the sea, and no winter would turn to Spring. Should she heed all we say of thrift, how many of us would be breathing this air?
plain: If nature listened to our talk of contentment, no river would seek the sea and no winter would become spring; if it listened to our talk of thrift, how many of us would even be alive?
core_idea: Nature ignores our talk of contentment and thrift

text: You see but your shadow when you turn your back to the sun.
note: Turning from the light leaves only shadow

tags.when_helps: Someone fixated on the dark side of things who needs to turn toward the light.

display_text: You see but your shadow when you turn your back to the sun.
plain: When you turn your back on the sun, all you see is your own shadow.
core_idea: Turning from the light shows only your shadow

text: You are free before the sun of the day, and free before the stars of the night; And you are free when there is no sun and no moon and no star. You are even free when you close your eyes upon all there is. But you are a slave to him whom you love because you love him, And a slave to him who loves you because he loves you.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling the bonds of love as both a joy and a loss of freedom.

display_text: You are free before the sun of the day, and free before the stars of the night; And you are free when there is no sun and no moon and no star. You are even free when you close your eyes upon all there is. But you are a slave to him whom you love because you love him, And a slave to him who loves you because he loves you.
plain: You are free under the sun, the stars, and even in total darkness or with your eyes shut; but you are a slave to the one you love, and to the one who loves you.
core_idea: Love is the one bond that limits our freedom

plain_judge.issue: Drops "because you love him", the reason for the bondage.

text: We are all beggars at the gate of the temple, and each one of us receives his share of the bounty of the King when he enters the temple, and when he goes out. But we are all jealous of one another, which is another way of belittling the King.

tags.when_helps: Someone resenting others' blessings who needs to see that everyone receives a share.

display_text: We are all beggars at the gate of the temple, and each one of us receives his share of the bounty of the King when he enters the temple, and when he goes out. But we are all jealous of one another, which is another way of belittling the King.
plain: We are all beggars at the temple gate, each receiving a share of the King's gifts as he comes and goes; yet we envy one another, which belittles the King.
core_idea: Envying each other belittles the giver of all

text: You cannot consume beyond your appetite. The other half of the loaf belongs to the other person, and there should remain a little bread for the chance guest.
note: Taking only what we need; sharing the rest

tags.when_helps: Someone taking more than they need and forgetting what belongs to others.

display_text: You cannot consume beyond your appetite. The other half of the loaf belongs to the other person, and there should remain a little bread for the chance guest.
plain: You cannot eat more than your hunger allows; the other half of the loaf belongs to someone else, and a little should be left for an unexpected guest.
core_idea: Take only what you need and share the rest

text: If it were not for guests all houses would be graves.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose home feels empty, or who has stopped inviting people in.

display_text: If it were not for guests all houses would be graves.
plain: Without guests, every house would be like a grave.
core_idea: Hospitality keeps a home alive

text: I stopped my guest on the threshold and said, “Nay, wipe not your feet as you enter, but as you go out.”
note: Welcoming guests; let them leave something behind

tags.when_helps: A host who wants guests to leave carrying something good rather than leaving nothing behind.

display_text: I stopped my guest on the threshold and said, “Nay, wipe not your feet as you enter, but as you go out.”
plain: I stopped my guest at the door and said, do not wipe your feet when you come in, but when you leave.
core_idea: A guest should take nothing away from the house

text: Generosity is not in giving me that which I need more than you do, but it is in giving me that which you need more than I do.
note: True generosity gives what you need most

tags.when_helps: Someone who thinks of themselves as generous and wants to understand what real giving costs.

display_text: Generosity is not in giving me that which I need more than you do, but it is in giving me that which you need more than I do.
plain: Real generosity is not giving me what I need more than you, but giving me what you need more than I do.
core_idea: Generosity means giving what you yourself need

text: You are indeed charitable when you give, and while giving, turn your face away so that you may not see the shyness of the receiver.
note: Giving with tact, sparing the receiver's shame

tags.when_helps: Someone helping another person who wants to give without making them feel small.

display_text: You are indeed charitable when you give, and while giving, turn your face away so that you may not see the shyness of the receiver.
plain: You are truly charitable when you give while looking away, so you do not see the receiver's embarrassment.
core_idea: True charity spares the receiver's shame

text: The difference between the richest man and the poorest is but a day of hunger and an hour of thirst.
note: Rich and poor are not so different

tags.when_helps: Someone measuring themselves or others by wealth who needs a sense of proportion.

display_text: The difference between the richest man and the poorest is but a day of hunger and an hour of thirst.
plain: The difference between the richest and the poorest person is only a day of hunger and an hour of thirst.
core_idea: Rich and poor are separated by very little

text: We often borrow from our tomorrows to pay our debts to our yesterdays.
note: Living on borrowed time and old debts

tags.when_helps: Someone sacrificing their future to settle past debts, mistakes or obligations.

display_text: We often borrow from our tomorrows to pay our debts to our yesterdays.
plain: We often borrow from our future to pay off debts from our past.
core_idea: We spend our future paying for our past

text: I too am visited by angels and devils, but I get rid of them. When it is an angel I pray an old prayer, and he is bored; When it is a devil I commit an old sin, and he passes me by.
note: Dealing with temptation and piety humorously

tags.when_helps: Someone with a wry view of their own moral struggles who appreciates honest humour about them.

display_text: I too am visited by angels and devils, but I get rid of them. When it is an angel I pray an old prayer, and he is bored; When it is a devil I commit an old sin, and he passes me by.
plain: Angels and devils visit me too, but I get rid of them: I bore the angel with an old prayer, and the devil passes me by when I commit an old sin.
core_idea: Stale prayer and stale sin both drive visitors away

text: After all this is not a bad prison; but I do not like this wall between my cell and the next prisoner’s cell; Yet I assure you that I do not wish to reproach the warder nor the Builder of the prison.
note: Accepting life's limits; longing for connection

tags.when_helps: Someone making peace with life's limits while still wishing for closer connection with others.

display_text: After all this is not a bad prison; but I do not like this wall between my cell and the next prisoner’s cell; Yet I assure you that I do not wish to reproach the warder nor the Builder of the prison.
plain: This life is not a bad prison, though I dislike the wall between my cell and my neighbour's; yet I do not blame the guard or the Builder of the prison.
core_idea: Life is a fair prison, but walls divide us

plain_judge.issue: Adds the explicit "this life" reading of the prison.

text: Those who give you a serpent when you ask for a fish, may have nothing but serpents to give. It is then generosity on their part.

tags.when_helps: Someone hurt that others failed to give what they needed, ready to see the limits of what those people had.

display_text: Those who give you a serpent when you ask for a fish, may have nothing but serpents to give. It is then generosity on their part.
plain: People who give you a snake when you asked for a fish may have nothing but snakes to give; for them, that is generosity.
core_idea: People can only give what they have

text: Trickery succeeds sometimes, but it always commits suicide.

tags.when_helps: Someone cheated by another, or tempted to cheat, who needs to see that deceit defeats itself.

display_text: Trickery succeeds sometimes, but it always commits suicide.
plain: Trickery sometimes works, but it always ends up destroying itself.
core_idea: Trickery always destroys itself
override: Names suicide (figuratively / as something prevented); hidden from distress by the 8 Oct 2026 precedent for MN 144 and Walden; applied 11 Oct, Shailesh to confirm

text: You are truly a forgiver when you forgive murderers who never spill blood, thieves who never steal, and liars who utter no falsehood.
note: Forgiving hidden wrongs, not just open ones

tags.when_helps: Someone holding grudges over hidden or imagined wrongs, asked what forgiveness really means.

display_text: You are truly a forgiver when you forgive murderers who never spill blood, thieves who never steal, and liars who utter no falsehood.
plain: You truly forgive when you forgive murderers who never shed blood, thieves who never steal, and liars who never say anything false.
core_idea: True forgiveness reaches hidden, unspoken wrongs

text: He who can put his finger upon that which divides good from evil is he who can touch the very hem of the garment of God.
note: The difficulty of telling good from evil

tags.when_helps: Someone wrestling with a moral dilemma where right and wrong are hard to separate.

display_text: He who can put his finger upon that which divides good from evil is he who can touch the very hem of the garment of God.
plain: Whoever can point to the line between good and evil can touch the hem of God's garment.
core_idea: Knowing good from evil brings one near God

text: If your heart is a volcano how shall you expect flowers to bloom in your hands?

tags.when_helps: Someone whose anger is spoiling what they try to build or give.

display_text: If your heart is a volcano how shall you expect flowers to bloom in your hands?
plain: If your heart is a volcano, how can you expect flowers to grow in your hands?
core_idea: An angry heart cannot produce gentle deeds

text: A strange form of self-indulgence! There are times when I would be wronged and cheated, that I may laugh at the expense of those who think I do not know I am being wronged and cheated.

tags.when_helps: Someone being cheated who chooses quiet amusement over anger.

display_text: A strange form of self-indulgence! There are times when I would be wronged and cheated, that I may laugh at the expense of those who think I do not know I am being wronged and cheated.
plain: A strange kind of indulgence: sometimes I would let myself be wronged and cheated so I can laugh at those who think I do not know it.
core_idea: Letting yourself be cheated can hold secret amusement

text: Let him who wipes his soiled hands with your garment take your garment. He may need it again; surely you would not.
note: Letting go when others misuse you

tags.when_helps: Someone who has been used or taken from, considering letting it go.

display_text: Let him who wipes his soiled hands with your garment take your garment. He may need it again; surely you would not.
plain: If someone wipes their dirty hands on your coat, let them keep the coat; they may need it again, and you surely will not.
core_idea: Let go of what others have soiled

text: Please do not whitewash your inherent faults with your acquired virtues. I would have the faults; they are like mine own.
note: Preferring honest faults to masked virtues

tags.when_helps: Someone hiding their flaws behind a polished image who needs permission to be real.

display_text: Please do not whitewash your inherent faults with your acquired virtues. I would have the faults; they are like mine own.
plain: Please do not cover up your natural faults with virtues you have acquired; I would rather have the faults, since they are like my own.
core_idea: Honest faults are better than borrowed virtues

text: How often have I attributed to myself crimes I have never committed, so that the other person may feel comfortable in my presence.
note: Humbling oneself so others feel at ease

tags.when_helps: Someone who belittles themselves to put others at ease and wonders why they do it.

display_text: How often have I attributed to myself crimes I have never committed, so that the other person may feel comfortable in my presence.
plain: How often I have claimed crimes I never committed so that another person could feel at ease with me.
core_idea: Admitting imagined faults can put others at ease

text: Even the masks of life are masks of deeper mystery.
note: The mystery behind the masks people wear

tags.when_helps: Someone puzzled by the roles people play, looking for what lies beneath them.

display_text: Even the masks of life are masks of deeper mystery.
plain: Even the masks life wears hide a deeper mystery.
core_idea: Life's masks conceal deeper mystery

text: You may judge others only according to your knowledge of yourself. Tell me now, who among us is guilty and who is unguilty? The truly just is he who feels half guilty of your misdeeds.

tags.when_helps: Someone quick to judge another's wrongdoing, invited to recognise their own share in it.

display_text: You may judge others only according to your knowledge of yourself. Tell me now, who among us is guilty and who is unguilty? The truly just is he who feels half guilty of your misdeeds.
plain: You can judge others only by what you know of yourself; so who is guilty and who is innocent? The truly just person feels half guilty for your wrongdoing.
core_idea: Judge others by yourself and share their guilt

text: It is only when you are pursued that you become swift.
note: Pressure makes us faster and stronger

tags.when_helps: Someone under pressure who needs to see that pressure can make them stronger and quicker.

display_text: It is only when you are pursued that you become swift.
plain: Only when something is chasing you do you become fast.
core_idea: Pressure makes us swift

text: I have no enemies, O God, but if I am to have an enemy Let his strength be equal to mine, That truth alone may be the victor.
note: Wishing for a fair fight with an enemy

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone facing a rival or conflict who wants a fair contest where truth wins.

display_text: I have no enemies, O God, but if I am to have an enemy Let his strength be equal to mine, That truth alone may be the victor.
plain: O God, I have no enemies, but if I must have one, let him be as strong as I am, so that only truth wins.
core_idea: Wish for an equal opponent so truth prevails

text: You will be quite friendly with your enemy when you both die.

tags.when_helps: Someone holding onto a long feud, reminded how small it looks beside mortality.

display_text: You will be quite friendly with your enemy when you both die.
plain: You and your enemy will get along well once you are both dead.
core_idea: Death ends all enmity

text: Long ago there lived a Man who was crucified for being too loving and too lovable. And strange to relate I met him thrice yesterday. The first time He was asking a policeman not to take a prostitute to prison; the second time He was drinking wine with an outcast; and the third time He was having a fist-fight with a promoter inside a church.

tags.when_helps: Someone disillusioned with religious hypocrisy who longs for faith lived as love for outcasts.

display_text: Long ago there lived a Man who was crucified for being too loving and too lovable. And strange to relate I met him thrice yesterday. The first time He was asking a policeman not to take a prostitute to prison; the second time He was drinking wine with an outcast; and the third time He was having a fist-fight with a promoter inside a church.
plain: A Man crucified long ago for being too loving was seen three times yesterday: asking police to spare a prostitute, drinking wine with an outcast, and fighting a promoter inside a church.
core_idea: Christ's love still sides with the outcast against the profiteer

plain_judge.issue: "Was seen" drops the narrator's own strange meeting with him.

text: If all they say of good and evil were true, then my life is but one long crime.
note: Conventional morality feels like an accusation

tags.when_helps: Someone weighed down by rigid moral rules that leave them feeling always in the wrong.

display_text: If all they say of good and evil were true, then my life is but one long crime.
plain: If everything people say about good and evil were true, my whole life would be one long crime.
core_idea: Conventional morality would condemn every life

text: Pity is but half justice.
note: Pity is not enough; justice is needed

tags.when_helps: Someone offered sympathy, or offering it, when real fairness is what is needed.

display_text: Pity is but half justice.
plain: Pity is only half of justice.
core_idea: Pity falls short of justice

text: The only one who has been unjust to me is the one to whose brother I have been unjust.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling wronged who is ready to consider the harm they have caused others.

display_text: The only one who has been unjust to me is the one to whose brother I have been unjust.
plain: The only person who has wronged me is the one whose brother I wronged first.
core_idea: The wrongs done to us echo the wrongs we did

plain_judge.issue: Adds 'first', implying the speaker wronged first; the original sets no order.

text: When you see a man led to prison say in your heart, “Mayhap he is escaping from a narrower prison.” And when you see a man drunken say in your heart, “Mayhap he sought escape from something still more unbeautiful.”

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone judging a person in prison or addiction, or watching a loved one struggle with either.

display_text: When you see a man led to prison say in your heart, “Mayhap he is escaping from a narrower prison.” And when you see a man drunken say in your heart, “Mayhap he sought escape from something still more unbeautiful.”
plain: When you see someone taken to prison, think that perhaps they are escaping a narrower prison; when you see someone drunk, think that perhaps they were fleeing something even uglier.
core_idea: Assume hidden suffering behind others' failings

text: Oftentimes I have hated in self-defense; but if I were stronger I would not have used such a weapon.

tags.when_helps: Someone who has hated those who hurt them and wonders whether there is a stronger way.

display_text: Oftentimes I have hated in self-defense; but if I were stronger I would not have used such a weapon.
plain: I have often hated to protect myself, but if I were stronger I would not have needed that weapon.
core_idea: Hatred is a weapon of the weak

plain_judge.issue: 'Would not have needed' replaces 'would not have used'; shifts from choice to necessity.

text: How stupid is he who would patch the hatred in his eyes with the smile of his lips.

tags.when_helps: Someone masking hostility behind politeness who needs to face it honestly.

display_text: How stupid is he who would patch the hatred in his eyes with the smile of his lips.
plain: How foolish is the person who tries to cover the hatred in their eyes with a smile.
core_idea: A smile cannot hide hatred in the eyes

text: Only those beneath me can envy or hate me. I have never been envied nor hated; I am above no one. Only those above me can praise or belittle me. I have never been praised nor belittled; I am below no one.

tags.when_helps: Someone caught up in comparison, rank and others' praise or contempt.

display_text: Only those beneath me can envy or hate me. I have never been envied nor hated; I am above no one. Only those above me can praise or belittle me. I have never been praised nor belittled; I am below no one.
plain: Only those beneath me can envy or hate me, and only those above me can praise or belittle me; since none of this happens to me, I am above and below no one.
core_idea: I stand equal to everyone, neither above nor below

text: Your saying to me, “I do not understand you,” is praise beyond my worth, and an insult you do not deserve.
note: Being told you are not understood

tags.when_helps: Someone told they are hard to understand, unsure whether to feel flattered or hurt.

display_text: Your saying to me, “I do not understand you,” is praise beyond my worth, and an insult you do not deserve.
plain: When you tell me you do not understand me, it is both more praise than I deserve and an insult you do not deserve.
core_idea: Not being understood is both praise and insult

text: How mean am I when life gives me gold and I give you silver, and yet I deem myself generous.

tags.when_helps: Someone who thinks of themselves as generous, invited to honest self-examination about it.

display_text: How mean am I when life gives me gold and I give you silver, and yet I deem myself generous.
plain: How petty I am when life gives me gold and I give you silver, yet I think of myself as generous.
core_idea: We give less than we receive yet feel generous

text: When you reach the heart of life you will find yourself not higher than the felon, and not lower than the prophet.
note: Equality of all at life's heart

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling either superior or worthless who needs a sense of shared humanity.

display_text: When you reach the heart of life you will find yourself not higher than the felon, and not lower than the prophet.
plain: When you reach the heart of life, you will find you are no higher than a criminal and no lower than a prophet.
