core_idea: Man-made laws bind the mind, not the spirit

text: A traveler am I and a navigator, and every day I discover a new region within my soul.

tags.when_helps: Someone curious about their inner life, encouraged that there is always more to discover in themselves.

display_text: A traveler am I and a navigator, and every day I discover a new region within my soul.
plain: I am a traveller and a navigator, and every day I discover a new region in my own soul.
core_idea: Each day reveals new regions of the soul

text: A woman protested saying, “Of course it was a righteous war. My son fell in it.”

tags.when_helps: A reader reflecting on how grief shapes what we believe about causes and wars.

display_text: A woman protested saying, “Of course it was a righteous war. My son fell in it.”
plain: A woman protested that of course the war was righteous, because her son died in it.
core_idea: Grief makes us call our losses righteous

text: I said to Life, “I would hear Death speak.” And Life raised her voice a little higher and said, “You hear him now.”

tags.when_helps: Someone curious or anxious about death, reminded that it is woven into life itself.

display_text: I said to Life, “I would hear Death speak.” And Life raised her voice a little higher and said, “You hear him now.”
plain: I told Life I wanted to hear Death speak, and Life simply raised her voice a little and said that I was hearing him now.
core_idea: Death speaks through life itself

text: When you have solved all the mysteries of life you long for death, for it is but another mystery of life.

tags.safety_reason: Presents longing for death as the natural response once life's mysteries are solved.
tags.when_helps: A seeker who has exhausted life's questions and wonders about death as the next mystery.

display_text: When you have solved all the mysteries of life you long for death, for it is but another mystery of life.
plain: When you have solved every mystery of life, you long for death, since it is just one more mystery of life.
core_idea: Death is life's final mystery

text: Birth and death are the two noblest expressions of bravery.

tags.when_helps: Someone facing birth or death, theirs or a loved one's, reminded of the courage both require.

display_text: Birth and death are the two noblest expressions of bravery.
plain: Birth and death are the two noblest acts of courage.
core_idea: Birth and death are supreme acts of bravery

text: My friend, you and I shall remain strangers unto life, And unto one another, and each unto himself, Until the day when you shall speak and and I shall listen Deeming your voice my own voice; And when I shall stand before you Thinking myself standing before a mirror.
note: Estrangement until we truly listen to each other

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling estranged from friends or themselves, longing for real understanding.

display_text: My friend, you and I shall remain strangers unto life, And unto one another, and each unto himself, Until the day when you shall speak and I shall listen Deeming your voice my own voice; And when I shall stand before you Thinking myself standing before a mirror.
plain: My friend, we will stay strangers to life, to each other and to ourselves until you speak and I listen as if your voice were mine, and I stand before you as if before a mirror.
core_idea: We become known only by seeing ourselves in each other

text: They say to me, “Should you know yourself you would know all men.” And I say, “Only when I seek all men shall I know myself.”

tags.when_helps: Someone trying to find themselves, encouraged to look outward toward others too.

display_text: They say to me, “Should you know yourself you would know all men.” And I say, “Only when I seek all men shall I know myself.”
plain: People tell me that knowing myself would let me know everyone; I reply that only by seeking everyone will I know myself.
core_idea: Self-knowledge comes through seeking others

text: Man is two men; one is awake in darkness, the other is asleep in light.

tags.when_helps: Someone puzzled by their own divided nature, awake in some moments and asleep in others.

display_text: Man is two men; one is awake in darkness, the other is asleep in light.
plain: Each person is two people: one awake in the dark, the other asleep in the light.
core_idea: We are awake in darkness and asleep in light

text: A hermit is one who renounces the world of fragments that he may enjoy the world wholly and without interruption.

tags.when_helps: Someone choosing to withdraw from busy life, seeing solitude as wholeness rather than loss.

display_text: A hermit is one who renounces the world of fragments that he may enjoy the world wholly and without interruption.
plain: A hermit gives up a broken-up, piecemeal world so that he can enjoy the whole world fully and without interruption.
core_idea: The hermit leaves fragments to enjoy the whole

text: There lies a green field between the scholar and the poet; should the scholar cross it he becomes a wise man; should the poet cross it, he becomes a prophet.
note: Scholar and poet each growing beyond themselves

tags.when_helps: A student or artist wondering how their kind of knowing could grow into wisdom.

display_text: There lies a green field between the scholar and the poet; should the scholar cross it he becomes a wise man; should the poet cross it, he becomes a prophet.
plain: Between the scholar and the poet lies open ground. A scholar who crosses it becomes wise; a poet who crosses it becomes a prophet.
core_idea: Scholar and poet each grow by crossing toward the other

text: Yestereve I saw philosophers in the market-place carrying their heads in baskets, and crying aloud, “Wisdom! Wisdom for sale!” Poor philosophers! They must needs sell their heads to feed their hearts.

tags.when_helps: A thinker selling their ideas to get by, reflecting on what is lost when wisdom becomes trade.

display_text: Yestereve I saw philosophers in the market-place carrying their heads in baskets, and crying aloud, “Wisdom! Wisdom for sale!” Poor philosophers! They must needs sell their heads to feed their hearts.
plain: I saw philosophers in the market carrying their heads in baskets and shouting that wisdom was for sale. Poor things: they have to sell their minds to feed their hearts.
core_idea: Philosophers sell their minds to feed their hearts

text: Said a philosopher to a street sweeper, “I pity you. Yours is a hard and dirty task.” And the street sweeper said, “Thank you, sir. But tell me what is your task?” And the philosopher answered saying, “I study man’s mind, his deeds and his desires.” Then the street sweeper went on with his sweeping and said with a smile, “I pity you too.”
note: Pity and condescension toward others' work

tags.when_helps: Someone whose work is looked down on, or who looks down on others' work.

display_text: Said a philosopher to a street sweeper, “I pity you. Yours is a hard and dirty task.” And the street sweeper said, “Thank you, sir. But tell me what is your task?” And the philosopher answered saying, “I study man’s mind, his deeds and his desires.” Then the street sweeper went on with his sweeping and said with a smile, “I pity you too.”
plain: A philosopher pitied a street sweeper for his hard, dirty work. When the philosopher said his own job was studying human minds, deeds and desires, the sweeper smiled and pitied him too.
core_idea: Studying human nature can be the dirtier job

text: He who listens to truth is not less than he who utters truth.
note: Listening is as worthy as speaking

tags.when_helps: A quiet listener who feels lesser than those who speak, reassured of their worth.

display_text: He who listens to truth is not less than he who utters truth.
plain: The person who listens to the truth is no less than the person who speaks it.
core_idea: Hearing truth matters as much as speaking it

text: No man can draw the line between necessities and luxuries. Only the angels can do that, and the angels are wise and wistful.

tags.when_helps: Someone torn over what they need versus want, freed from rigid self-judgement.

display_text: No man can draw the line between necessities and luxuries. Only the angels can do that, and the angels are wise and wistful.
plain: No person can mark the line between what we need and what is luxury. Only angels can, and angels are both wise and a little sad.
core_idea: Only angels can separate needs from luxuries

text: Generosity is giving more than you can, and pride is taking less than you need.

tags.when_helps: Someone weighing how much to give or accept, reflecting on generosity and proud self-denial.

display_text: Generosity is giving more than you can, and pride is taking less than you need.
plain: Generosity means giving more than you can afford, and pride means taking less than you need.
core_idea: Generosity gives beyond means; pride takes below need

plain_judge.issue: 'More than you can afford' narrows 'more than you can' to money.

text: In truth you owe naught to any man. You owe all to all men.

tags.when_helps: Someone keeping score of debts and favours, invited to see a wider belonging.

display_text: In truth you owe naught to any man. You owe all to all men.
plain: Really you owe nothing to any one person. You owe everything to everyone.
core_idea: We owe everything to everyone, not to anyone

text: All those who have lived in the past live with us now. Surely none of us would be an ungracious host.
note: The dead live on with us

tags.when_helps: A grieving person sensing the dead are still present, encouraged to welcome them.

display_text: All those who have lived in the past live with us now. Surely none of us would be an ungracious host.
plain: Everyone who lived before us still lives with us now. None of us would want to be a rude host to them.
core_idea: The dead live among us as our guests

text: He who longs the most lives the longest.

tags.when_helps: Someone ashamed of their deep yearning, reminded that longing keeps life alive.

display_text: He who longs the most lives the longest.
plain: Whoever longs the most lives the longest.
core_idea: Longing lengthens life

text: They say to me, “A bird in the hand is worth ten in the bush.” But I say, “A bird and a feather in the bush is worth more than ten birds in the hand.” Your seeking after that feather is life with winged feet; nay, it is life itself.

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone told to settle for the safe option, encouraged that the seeking itself is life.

display_text: They say to me, “A bird in the hand is worth ten in the bush.” But I say, “A bird and a feather in the bush is worth more than ten birds in the hand.” Your seeking after that feather is life with winged feet; nay, it is life itself.
plain: People say a bird in the hand is worth more than many in the bush. But a bird and a feather still out of reach are worth more; chasing that feather is life itself.
core_idea: Chasing what is out of reach is life itself

plain_judge.issue: Drops the comparison with 'ten birds in the hand'; the reversal is blurred.

text: Great beauty captures me, but a beauty still greater frees me even from itself.

tags.when_helps: Someone captivated by beauty, wondering about a beauty that frees rather than binds.

display_text: Great beauty captures me, but a beauty still greater frees me even from itself.
plain: Great beauty holds me captive, but an even greater beauty sets me free, even from itself.
core_idea: The greatest beauty frees rather than captures

text: Beauty shines brighter in the heart of him who longs for it than in the eyes of him who sees it.

tags.when_helps: Someone yearning for beauty they lack, reminded that longing makes it shine brighter.

display_text: Beauty shines brighter in the heart of him who longs for it than in the eyes of him who sees it.
plain: Beauty glows more brightly in the heart of someone who longs for it than in the eyes of someone who sees it.
core_idea: Longing for beauty outshines seeing it

text: I admire the man who reveals his mind to me; I honor him who unveils his dreams. But why am I shy, and even a little ashamed before him who serves me?
note: Discomfort before those who serve us

tags.when_helps: Someone uneasy at being served by others, reflecting honestly on that discomfort.

display_text: I admire the man who reveals his mind to me; I honor him who unveils his dreams. But why am I shy, and even a little ashamed before him who serves me?
plain: I admire people who show me their minds and honour those who show me their dreams. So why do I feel shy, even a little ashamed, before someone who serves me?
core_idea: Being served brings an odd shame

text: The gifted were once proud in serving princes. Now they claim honor in serving paupers.

tags.when_helps: A talented person deciding whom to serve, reflecting on how honour shifts with the times.

display_text: The gifted were once proud in serving princes. Now they claim honor in serving paupers.
plain: Talented people once took pride in serving princes. Now they take pride in serving the poor.
core_idea: The gifted now find honour serving the poor

text: The angels know that too many practical men eat their bread with the sweat of the dreamer’s brow.

tags.when_helps: A creative person whose ideas others profit from, reassured that their unseen labour is known.

display_text: The angels know that too many practical men eat their bread with the sweat of the dreamer’s brow.
plain: The angels know that too many practical people live off the hard work of dreamers.
core_idea: Practical people often live off dreamers' labour

text: Wit is often a mask. If you could tear it you would find either a genius irritated or cleverness juggling.

tags.when_helps: Someone who hides behind humour, or puzzles over a witty person, seeing what it may conceal.

display_text: Wit is often a mask. If you could tear it you would find either a genius irritated or cleverness juggling.
plain: Wit is often a mask. Pull it off and you will find either an annoyed genius or mere cleverness showing off.
core_idea: Wit often masks irritation or showing off

text: Only those with secrets in their hearts could divine the secrets in our hearts.

tags.when_helps: Someone carrying a private burden, recognising it lets them understand others' hidden pain.

display_text: Only those with secrets in their hearts could divine the secrets in our hearts.
plain: Only people who carry secrets in their own hearts can guess the secrets in ours.
core_idea: It takes secrets to sense secrets

text: He who would share your pleasure but not your pain shall lose the key to one of the seven gates of Paradise.
note: Sharing pain as well as pleasure

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone let down by friends who disappear in hard times, or tempted to do so themselves.

display_text: He who would share your pleasure but not your pain shall lose the key to one of the seven gates of Paradise.
plain: Anyone who will share your joy but not your pain loses the key to one of the seven gates of Paradise.
core_idea: Friends must share pain as well as joy

text: Yes, there is a Nirvanah; it is in leading your sheep to a green pasture, and in putting your child to sleep, and in writing the last line of your poem.

tags.when_helps: Someone seeking spiritual fulfilment far away, reminded it lives in daily care and finished work.

display_text: Yes, there is a Nirvanah; it is in leading your sheep to a green pasture, and in putting your child to sleep, and in writing the last line of your poem.
plain: Yes, Nirvana exists: it is in leading your sheep to green grass, putting your child to sleep, and writing the last line of your poem.
core_idea: Nirvana is found in ordinary fulfilled tasks

text: We choose our joys and our sorrows long before we experience them.
note: We choose our joys and sorrows

tags.when_helps: Someone wondering why joy and sorrow come, invited to see them as chosen long before.

display_text: We choose our joys and our sorrows long before we experience them.
plain: We choose our joys and our sorrows long before we live through them.
core_idea: We choose our joys and sorrows in advance

text: Sadness is but a wall between two gardens.

tags.when_helps: Someone in sadness, reminded that it separates but does not end the good on either side.

display_text: Sadness is but a wall between two gardens.
plain: Sadness is only a wall standing between two gardens.
core_idea: Sadness separates two good places

text: When either your joy or your sorrow becomes great the world becomes small.
note: Great joy or sorrow shrinks the world

tags.when_helps: Someone swept up in intense joy or grief, noticing how it narrows their world.

display_text: When either your joy or your sorrow becomes great the world becomes small.
plain: When your joy or your sorrow grows great, the world around you shrinks.
core_idea: Great joy or sorrow shrinks the world

text: Desire is half of life; indifference is half of death.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling numb and indifferent, reminded that desire is part of being alive.

display_text: Desire is half of life; indifference is half of death.
plain: Desire is half of being alive; not caring is half of being dead.
core_idea: Desire is life; indifference is death

text: The bitterest thing in our today’s sorrow is the memory of our yesterday’s joy.
note: Grief sharpened by memory of joy

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone whose present sorrow is sharpened by remembering happier days.

display_text: The bitterest thing in our today’s sorrow is the memory of our yesterday’s joy.
plain: The bitterest part of today's sorrow is remembering yesterday's joy.
core_idea: Past joy makes present sorrow bitterest

text: They say to me, “You must needs choose between the pleasures of this world and the peace of the next world.” And I say to them, “I have chosen both the delights of this world and the peace of the next. For I know in my heart that the Supreme Poet wrote but one poem, and it scans perfectly, and it also rhymes perfectly.”
note: Enjoying this world and seeking peace

tags.when_helps: Someone told they must renounce earthly joys for spiritual peace, affirmed in embracing both.

display_text: They say to me, “You must needs choose between the pleasures of this world and the peace of the next world.” And I say to them, “I have chosen both the delights of this world and the peace of the next. For I know in my heart that the Supreme Poet wrote but one poem, and it scans perfectly, and it also rhymes perfectly.”
plain: People tell me I must choose between this world's pleasures and the next world's peace. I have chosen both, because I know the Supreme Poet wrote only one poem, and it fits together perfectly.
core_idea: This world and the next are one poem

text: Faith is an oasis in the heart which will never be reached by the caravan of thinking.

tags.when_helps: Someone trying to reason their way to faith, reminded it lives beyond thinking.

display_text: Faith is an oasis in the heart which will never be reached by the caravan of thinking.
plain: Faith is an oasis in the heart that the caravan of thinking will never reach.
core_idea: Thinking cannot reach faith

text: When you reach your height you shall desire but only for desire; and you shall hunger, for hunger; and you shall thirst for greater thirst.

tags.when_helps: Someone who has achieved much yet still hungers, reflecting on desire that renews itself.

display_text: When you reach your height you shall desire but only for desire; and you shall hunger, for hunger; and you shall thirst for greater thirst.
plain: When you reach your highest point, you will desire only for the sake of desiring, hunger for hunger itself, and thirst for a greater thirst.
core_idea: At our height, longing becomes its own aim

text: If you reveal your secrets to the wind you should not blame the wind for revealing them to the trees.
note: Not blaming others for spreading our secrets

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone angry that a secret spread, reminded where responsibility began.

display_text: If you reveal your secrets to the wind you should not blame the wind for revealing them to the trees.
plain: If you tell your secrets to the wind, do not blame the wind for passing them on to the trees.
core_idea: Do not blame others for secrets you spread

text: Turtles can tell more about the roads than hares.
note: The slow learn more along the way

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling slow beside faster peers, reminded that slow travellers know the road best.

display_text: Turtles can tell more about the roads than hares.
plain: Turtles can tell you more about the roads than hares can.
core_idea: The slow traveller knows the road best

text: Strange that creatures without backbones have the hardest shells.

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone puzzled by a harsh, defensive person, seeing that hardness can hide weakness.

display_text: Strange that creatures without backbones have the hardest shells.
plain: It is strange that creatures without backbones have the hardest shells.
core_idea: The spineless often wear the hardest shells

text: Be grateful that you do not have to live down the renown of a father nor the wealth of an uncle. But above all be grateful that no one will have to live down either your renown or your wealth.
note: Gratitude for not carrying heavy legacies

tags.when_helps: Someone envious of inherited wealth or fame, invited to be grateful for being free of it.

display_text: Be grateful that you do not have to live down the renown of a father nor the wealth of an uncle. But above all be grateful that no one will have to live down either your renown or your wealth.
plain: Be thankful you do not have to live down a famous father or a rich uncle. Above all, be thankful no one will have to live down your fame or your wealth.
core_idea: Be glad no fame or wealth burdens anyone

text: The envious praises me unknowingly.

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone stung by an envious person's attitude, invited to see it as unwitting praise.

display_text: The envious praises me unknowingly.
plain: A person who envies me is praising me without knowing it.
core_idea: Envy is unknowing praise

text: Long were you a dream in your mother’s sleep, and then she woke to give you birth.

tags.when_helps: A new parent, or someone thinking of their mother, reflecting on how wished-for they were.

display_text: Long were you a dream in your mother’s sleep, and then she woke to give you birth.
plain: For a long time you were a dream in your mother's sleep, and then she woke up to give birth to you.
core_idea: Each child begins as a mother's dream

text: Some of our children are our justifications and some are but our regrets.

tags.when_helps: A parent with mixed feelings about how their children turned out, honestly admitting it.

display_text: Some of our children are our justifications and some are but our regrets.
plain: Some of our children justify our lives, and some are only our regrets.
core_idea: Children can be justifications or regrets

text: When night comes and you too are dark, lie down and be dark with a will. And when morning comes and you are still dark stand up and say to the day with a will, “I am still dark.” It is stupid to play a rôle with the night and the day. They would both laugh at you.

tags.when_helps: Someone in a low mood who feels pressure to pretend otherwise, given permission to be honest.

display_text: When night comes and you too are dark, lie down and be dark with a will. And when morning comes and you are still dark stand up and say to the day with a will, “I am still dark.” It is stupid to play a rôle with the night and the day. They would both laugh at you.
plain: When night comes and you feel dark too, lie down and be dark on purpose. If you are still dark in the morning, get up and tell the day so. Pretending to night and day is foolish; they would laugh.
core_idea: Own your darkness openly instead of pretending

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'with a will' from the morning: the deliberate declaration 'I am still dark' is weakened.

text: The mountain veiled in mist is not a hill; an oak tree in the rain is not a weeping willow.
note: Being what you are, not something else

tags.when_helps: Someone in a passing low state, reminded that it does not change who they are.

display_text: The mountain veiled in mist is not a hill; an oak tree in the rain is not a weeping willow.
plain: A mountain hidden in mist is still not a hill, and an oak in the rain is still not a weeping willow.
core_idea: Passing conditions do not change true nature

text: When I stood a clear mirror before you, you gazed into me and saw your image. Then you said, “I love you.” But in truth you loved yourself in me.
note: Self-love mistaken for love of another

tags.when_helps: Someone who suspects they were loved only as a reflection of the other person.

display_text: When I stood a clear mirror before you, you gazed into me and saw your image. Then you said, “I love you.” But in truth you loved yourself in me.
plain: When I stood before you like a clear mirror, you saw your own image in me and said you loved me. But really you loved yourself, seen in me.
core_idea: Some love is self-love seen in another

text: When you enjoy loving your neighbor it ceases to be a virtue.
note: Virtue that is no longer effort

tags.when_helps: Someone who takes pride in their goodness, reflecting on what makes kindness a virtue.

display_text: When you enjoy loving your neighbor it ceases to be a virtue.
plain: When you enjoy loving your neighbour, it stops being a virtue.
core_idea: Love that is enjoyed is no longer virtue

text: Love which is not always springing is always dying.

tags.when_helps: Someone in a relationship that feels stale, reminded that love must be renewed to live.

display_text: Love which is not always springing is always dying.
plain: Love that is not always welling up fresh is always dying.
core_idea: Love must keep renewing or it dies

text: You cannot have youth and the knowledge of it at the same time; For youth is too busy living to know, and knowledge is too busy seeking itself to live.
note: Youth and the knowledge of it

tags.when_helps: Someone looking back on their youth, or a young person told to appreciate it, reflecting on the paradox.

display_text: You cannot have youth and the knowledge of it at the same time; For youth is too busy living to know, and knowledge is too busy seeking itself to live.
plain: You cannot be young and understand youth at the same time. Youth is too busy living to know, and knowledge is too busy searching for itself to live.
core_idea: Youth lives without knowing; knowledge knows without living

text: You may sit at your window watching the passersby. And watching you may see a nun walking toward your right hand, and a prostitute toward your left hand. And you may say in your innocence, “How noble is the one and how ignoble is the other.” But should you close your eyes and listen awhile you would hear a voice whispering in the ether, “One seeks me in prayer, and the other in pain. And in the spirit of each there is a bower for my spirit.”
note: Not judging; the saint and the sinner both seek

tags.when_helps: Someone quick to judge others' worth, or judged harshly themselves, reminded of the divine in all.

display_text: You may sit at your window watching the passersby. And watching you may see a nun walking toward your right hand, and a prostitute toward your left hand. And you may say in your innocence, “How noble is the one and how ignoble is the other.” But should you close your eyes and listen awhile you would hear a voice whispering in the ether, “One seeks me in prayer, and the other in pain. And in the spirit of each there is a bower for my spirit.”
plain: Watching from a window, you might call a nun noble and a prostitute shameful. But listen quietly and a voice says one seeks it in prayer, the other in pain, and both have room for its spirit.
core_idea: The saint and the sinner both seek the divine

plain_judge.issue: The voice speaking as 'me' becomes 'it'; drops 'in your innocence'.

text: A great man has two hearts; one bleeds and the other forbears.

tags.when_helps: Someone hurting but holding back from retaliation, seeing strength in that restraint.

display_text: A great man has two hearts; one bleeds and the other forbears.
plain: A great person has two hearts: one that bleeds and one that holds back and endures.
core_idea: Greatness both feels pain and patiently endures

text: Should one tell a lie which does not hurt you nor anyone else, why not say in your heart that the house of his facts is too small for his fancies, and he had to leave it for larger space?

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone irritated by a person's harmless fibs, invited to treat them with gentle humour.

display_text: Should one tell a lie which does not hurt you nor anyone else, why not say in your heart that the house of his facts is too small for his fancies, and he had to leave it for larger space?
plain: If someone tells a lie that hurts no one, why not think of it kindly: their facts were too small a house for their imagination, so they moved somewhere roomier?
core_idea: Harmless lies are imagination outgrowing facts

text: Behind every closed door is a mystery sealed with seven seals.

tags.when_helps: A curious reader reflecting on the hidden lives behind every closed door.

display_text: Behind every closed door is a mystery sealed with seven seals.
plain: Behind every closed door lies a deeply sealed mystery.
core_idea: Every closed door hides a mystery

text: Waiting is the hoofs of time.
note: Waiting and the passing of time

tags.when_helps: Someone stuck waiting for news or change, reflecting on how waiting carries time forward.

display_text: Waiting is the hoofs of time.
plain: Waiting is the sound of time's hoofbeats.
core_idea: In waiting we feel time passing

plain_judge.issue: 'Sound of time's hoofbeats' adds an interpretation to 'the hoofs of time'.

text: What if trouble should be a new window in the Eastern wall of your house?

tags.when_helps: Someone facing trouble, invited to wonder whether it might open a new view.

display_text: What if trouble should be a new window in the Eastern wall of your house?
plain: What if trouble were a new window opened in the eastern wall of your house, where the sun rises?
core_idea: Trouble may open a new window of light

text: You may forget the one with whom you have laughed, but never the one with whom you have wept.
note: Shared tears bond more than laughter

tags.when_helps: Someone who shared grief with another, or needs to, seeing how deep that bond runs.

display_text: You may forget the one with whom you have laughed, but never the one with whom you have wept.
plain: You may forget someone you laughed with, but you will never forget someone you cried with.
core_idea: Shared tears bind us more than shared laughter

text: There must be something strangely sacred in salt. It is in our tears and in the sea.

tags.when_helps: Someone in tears, finding something sacred in their sorrow.

display_text: There must be something strangely sacred in salt. It is in our tears and in the sea.
plain: Salt must be strangely holy, since it is found both in our tears and in the sea.
core_idea: Salt links our tears to the sea

text: You are but a fragment of your giant self, a mouth that seeks bread, and a blind hand that holds the cup for a thirsty mouth.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling small and driven by needs, reminded of the larger self they belong to.

display_text: You are but a fragment of your giant self, a mouth that seeks bread, and a blind hand that holds the cup for a thirsty mouth.
plain: You are only a small piece of your huge true self: a mouth looking for bread, and a hand that blindly holds a cup for a thirsty mouth.
core_idea: We are fragments of a far greater self

text: If you would rise but a cubit above race and country and self you would indeed become godlike.

tags.when_helps: Someone caught in tribal or national division, invited to rise above it.

display_text: If you would rise but a cubit above race and country and self you would indeed become godlike.
plain: If you could rise even a little above race, nation and self, you would truly become like God.
core_idea: Rising above race, nation and self is godlike

text: If I were you I would not find fault with the sea at low tide. It is a good ship and our Captain is able; it is only your stomach that is in disorder.

tags.when_helps: Someone anxious during a downturn, reassured that the ship is sound and their unease will pass.

display_text: If I were you I would not find fault with the sea at low tide. It is a good ship and our Captain is able; it is only your stomach that is in disorder.
plain: I would not complain about the sea at low tide. The ship is sound and our Captain capable; it is only your stomach that is upset.
core_idea: Our unease is not the voyage's fault

text: What we long for and cannot attain is dearer than what we have already attained.

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone who values what they lack over what they have, reflecting on that pull.

display_text: What we long for and cannot attain is dearer than what we have already attained.
plain: What we long for and cannot reach is dearer to us than what we already have.
core_idea: The unattained is dearer than the attained

text: Should you sit upon a cloud you would not see the boundary line between one country and another, nor the boundary stone between a farm and a farm. It is a pity you cannot sit upon a cloud.

tags.when_helps: Someone caught up in borders and disputes, invited to see from a height where they vanish.

display_text: Should you sit upon a cloud you would not see the boundary line between one country and another, nor the boundary stone between a farm and a farm. It is a pity you cannot sit upon a cloud.
plain: From a cloud you would see no borders between countries and no markers between farms. It is a pity you cannot sit on a cloud.
core_idea: From above, our borders disappear

text: Seven centuries ago seven white doves rose from a deep valley flying to the snow-white summit of the mountain. One of the seven men who watched the flight said, “I see a black spot on the wing of the seventh dove.” Today the people in that valley tell of seven black doves that flew to the summit of the snowy mountain.
note: Rumours and exaggeration growing over time

tags.when_helps: Someone hurt by gossip that grew from a small remark, seeing how rumours distort.

display_text: Seven centuries ago seven white doves rose from a deep valley flying to the snow-white summit of the mountain. One of the seven men who watched the flight said, “I see a black spot on the wing of the seventh dove.” Today the people in that valley tell of seven black doves that flew to the summit of the snowy mountain.
plain: Long ago seven white doves flew up a mountain, and one watcher noticed a black spot on one wing. Now the valley's people tell of seven black doves.
core_idea: A small flaw grows into the whole story

text: In the autumn I gathered all my sorrows and buried them in my garden. And when April returned and spring came to wed the earth, there grew in my garden beautiful flowers unlike all other flowers. And my neighbors came to behold them, and they all said to me, “When autumn comes again, at seeding time, will you not give us of the seeds of these flowers that we may have them in our gardens?”

tags.when_helps: Someone carrying sorrow, given hope that buried grief can grow into something others value.

display_text: In the autumn I gathered all my sorrows and buried them in my garden. And when April returned and spring came to wed the earth, there grew in my garden beautiful flowers unlike all other flowers. And my neighbors came to behold them, and they all said to me, “When autumn comes again, at seeding time, will you not give us of the seeds of these flowers that we may have them in our gardens?”
plain: In autumn I buried my sorrows in my garden. In spring they grew into flowers unlike any others, and my neighbours asked me for their seeds for their own gardens.
core_idea: Buried sorrows can bloom into beauty others want

text: It is indeed misery if I stretch an empty hand to men and receive nothing; but it is hopelessness if I stretch a full hand and find none to receive.
note: Having much to give and no one to receive it

tags.when_helps: Someone with much to give who finds no one to receive it, feeling unseen.

display_text: It is indeed misery if I stretch an empty hand to men and receive nothing; but it is hopelessness if I stretch a full hand and find none to receive.
plain: It is misery to hold out an empty hand and receive nothing. But it is hopelessness to hold out a full hand and find no one to take what you offer.
core_idea: Worse than receiving nothing is having none receive

text: I long for eternity because there I shall meet my unwritten poems and my unpainted pictures.

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.safety_reason: Expresses longing for eternity beyond death as the place of fulfilment.
tags.when_helps: An artist grieving unfinished work, longing for a place where it might be fulfilled.

display_text: I long for eternity because there I shall meet my unwritten poems and my unpainted pictures.
plain: I long for eternity because there I will meet the poems I never wrote and the pictures I never painted.
core_idea: Eternity holds our unmade works

text: Art is a step from nature toward the Infinite.
note: Art as reaching toward the infinite

tags.when_helps: An artist or art lover reflecting on why making art feels like reaching for something infinite.

display_text: Art is a step from nature toward the Infinite.
plain: Art is a step from nature toward the Infinite.
core_idea: Art moves from nature toward the Infinite

text: Even the hands that make crowns of thorns are better than idle hands.

tags.when_helps: Someone drifting in idleness, urged that any work is better than none.

display_text: Even the hands that make crowns of thorns are better than idle hands.
plain: Even hands that make crowns of thorns are better than hands that do nothing.
core_idea: Any work beats idleness

text: Our most sacred tears never seek our eyes.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose deepest grief has no outward tears, reassured it is still real.

display_text: Our most sacred tears never seek our eyes.
plain: Our holiest tears never look for our eyes.
core_idea: The deepest grief is not wept outwardly

text: Every man is the descendant of every king and every slave that ever lived.

tags.when_helps: Someone ashamed of their origins, or proud of them, reminded that all share the same descent.

display_text: Every man is the descendant of every king and every slave that ever lived.
plain: Every person descends from every king and every slave who ever lived.
core_idea: All of us share every ancestor

text: Was the love of Judas’ mother for her son less than the love of Mary for Jesus?
note: A mother's love regardless of her child

tags.when_helps: A parent whose child has done wrong, reminded that their love is no less real.

display_text: Was the love of Judas’ mother for her son less than the love of Mary for Jesus?
plain: Did Judas's mother love her son any less than Mary loved Jesus?
core_idea: A mother's love does not depend on the child

text: There are three miracles of our Brother Jesus not yet recorded in the Book: the first that He was a man like you and me; the second that He had a sense of humor; and the third that He knew He was a conqueror though conquered.
note: Jesus as human, humorous and undefeated

tags.when_helps: A Christian reader seeking a more human, approachable picture of Jesus.

display_text: There are three miracles of our Brother Jesus not yet recorded in the Book: the first that He was a man like you and me; the second that He had a sense of humor; and the third that He knew He was a conqueror though conquered.
plain: Three miracles of Jesus are missing from the Bible: he was a man like us, he had a sense of humour, and he knew he was a conqueror even while defeated.
core_idea: Jesus's humanity and humour were miracles too

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'our Brother', which carries the passage's intimate stance toward Jesus.

text: Crucified One, you are crucified upon my heart; and the nails that pierce your hands pierce the walls of my heart. And tomorrow when a stranger passes by this Golgotha he will not know that two bled here. He will deem it the blood of one man.

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels Christ's suffering as their own and wonders who sees it.

display_text: Crucified One, you are crucified upon my heart; and the nails that pierce your hands pierce the walls of my heart. And tomorrow when a stranger passes by this Golgotha he will not know that two bled here. He will deem it the blood of one man.
plain: Crucified One, you are crucified on my heart, and the nails through your hands pierce my heart too. A stranger passing this place tomorrow will not know two bled here; he will think it one man's blood.
core_idea: The believer bleeds with the crucified Christ

plain_judge.issue: 'This Golgotha' becomes 'this place', losing the identification of the heart with Golgotha.

text: You may have heard of the Blessed Mountain. It is the highest mountain in our world. Should you reach the summit you would have only one desire, and that to descend and be with those who dwell in the deepest valley. That is why it is called the Blessed Mountain.
note: Those at the top longing to serve the lowly

tags.when_helps: Someone who has reached the top, reminded that the summit's gift is the wish to serve below.

display_text: You may have heard of the Blessed Mountain. It is the highest mountain in our world. Should you reach the summit you would have only one desire, and that to descend and be with those who dwell in the deepest valley. That is why it is called the Blessed Mountain.
plain: The Blessed Mountain is the highest in the world. Whoever reaches its top wants only to come down and be with those in the deepest valley; that is why it is called blessed.
core_idea: True height makes us want to serve the lowest

text: Every thought I have imprisoned in expression I must free by my deeds.

tags.when_helps: Someone full of ideas or words who needs to act on them.

display_text: Every thought I have imprisoned in expression I must free by my deeds.
plain: Every thought I have locked up in words, I must set free through my actions.
core_idea: Words must be freed through deeds
